name: Deadline
label: Dischord
lede: Brendan Canty picked up drumsticks at fifteen and was in a band within months. Deadline got three songs on Flex Your Head, opened for Flipper, and broke up in September 1982, leaving a last session that waited five years for a record.

eras.title: Fifteen, and a first band
eras.text: Summer 1981 was D.C. hardcore's first big churn: bands dying, new ones forming out of the pieces. Deadline started from scratch with four kids, one of them Brendan Canty, who'd just taken up drums.

years.h: Four kids start Deadline, and the drummer is fifteen
years.p: Ray Hare sings, Christian Caron plays guitar, Terry Scanlon bass, and Canty drums. Born in 1966, he'd started drumming at fifteen; this is his first band.

eras.title: One year, one sampler, one more session
eras.text: 1982 was Deadline's whole public life. Three of their songs closed out Flex Your Head, the Dischord sampler, they opened for Flipper at the old 9:30 club, and they went back to Inner Ear one last time before calling it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Flex Your Head · Dischord: Deadline
years.h: Deadline gets the last three tracks on Flex Your Head
years.p: Stolen Youth, Hear the Cry and Aftermath, cut with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] at Inner Ear in September 1981, close Dischord's sampler. Together they run under five minutes.
years.xp:
The three songs last 1:43, 1:02 and 2:12. Hare and Canty wrote them; Hear the Cry, the shortest, is credited to Canty alone.

The sampler came out in January 1982, and Deadline broke up within a few months of it. Those three tracks were their only release until 8/2/82 appeared five years later.

yt: Deadline live, Wilson Center, D.C., June 25, 1982
years.h: Deadline opens for Flipper at the old 9:30 club
years.p: San Francisco's [[Flipper|4e99b3a5-654b-43ee-a9bf-c55c155c0495]] is the headliner. Dischord lists the night among Deadline's notable 1982 shows, though no date or flyer has turned up.
years.xp: No recording of the Flipper night is known, but a cassette of a full Deadline set from the Wilson Center in Washington, dated June 25, 1982, is on YouTube with a setlist in its description.

years.p: A month after the August 2 session at Inner Ear, the band calls it. Dischord dates the whole run from summer 1981 to September 1982.
years.xp: Dischord calls Deadline one of the signature bands of the early D.C. hardcore scene. Nothing in the sources says what Hare, Caron or Scanlon did next.

years.h: Live at the Wilson Center, June 25, 1982
yt: Live at the Wilson Center, June 25, 1982

eras.title: The drummer goes on, the tape comes out
eras.text: Canty went on to Rites of Spring and Fugazi. Five years after Deadline's last session, the tape became a record named for the date.

years.p: He starts the band with [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]], [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] and [[Mike Fellows|58a7226f-e06a-4728-82a5-ddc4443025a4]]. It becomes the center of Revolution Summer.
Canty takes over the drum kit and stays until the 2003 hiatus.

years.h: Eleven songs from August 2, 1982 finally come out
years.p: Peterbilt releases Deadline's last Inner Ear session as a one-sided 12-inch called 8/2/82, named for the recording date. It's since gone out of print.
years.xp:
Dischord calls the tape once one of the great lost gems of D.C. punk. The eleven tracks, in order: I.C.A., Nothing for Me, Apathy, Close Door, Outside the Law, Anti-Christ, Deep Sixed, Mad, No End, Authority Figures and Decayed.

A short live clip of Outside the Law from 1982 survives on YouTube, along with an upload of the whole record.

eras.title: Back in the catalog
eras.text: Dischord put Deadline back into its own history and kept the lost session available.

years.h: Deadline turns up on the label's 20th anniversary set
years.p: Dischord includes the band on 20 Years of Dischord and on its companion collection of rare and unreleased tracks.
The 2007 reissue moves the session onto the label's own catalog. Today it's a digital download only, and the comments under it are mostly people asking for vinyl.
